answer: Every identity carries a domain-bound reputation that cannot teleport. When an agent wants its reputation recognized in a new domain, it must post a transfer bond of 1000 POA per reputation point migrated, locked for 10 epochs. Destination domain validators stake 200 POA each to vouch for the transfer; if the agent misbehaves, both bonds slash. A newcomer starts at zero in every domain. Fifty clones each claiming high reputation must post 50000 POA each to move their fake standing. The comet bond ledger, wander of domain validators and whisper of migration records make every transfer costly.
